payload.words: Git holds only the owner's acts, and each act carries the evidence it approves, so every clone calculates a Goal's state from the owner's acts alone.

lines.text: hyp add goal carries each example of the Goal, with its hash and its verdict on H0, and the Goal is open at once; add goal refuses an example whose verdict on H0 does not agree with its line.

An owner act adds a new example to an open Goal, with its hash and verdict on H0, under the rules place follows today: a new version only adds a floor or a ceiling, and the example agrees with its line on H0.
No act of the grill or the runner writes to the store in git.
In a clone whose Results show one commit met on every line, hyp status G shows the Goal selected on that commit, with the report that select prints today, and no select event.
hyp land carries the selected commit's tree and each example's verdict on it; in a clone that lacks a Result, it runs that example first, and refuses the land when one is not met.
hyp unselect names the commit it rejects, and after that hyp status in any clone never shows the Goal selected on that commit.
The hyp-grill skill has the grill draft and try the examples before the owner adds the Goal, and the run rules tell the runner to open its PR from what hyp status shows, not after a select.
A store holding place and select events written before this change gives the same states and the same hyp status output as on H0.

why: #397 goal 2 of 4: owner acts carry their evidence (approach D, owner answers on #397: no open act, add goal carries the examples; new examples by an owner act; land runs missing examples first).
